candidates.name: ZEROTOKYO
candidates.why: Tokyo's biggest new superclub, in Kabukicho Tower, a 5-minute walk from Garfield House. On the December calendar: Fri 18 Dec 'THE ONE presents Steve Angello' (house/progressive) and Sat 26 Dec 'NEON STARS' (bass/open format/techno). This is the headline club night for both Tokyo legs.
candidates.best_time: Doors 23:00, peak 00:30–03:30; go after dinner at Kabuki Hall downstairs
candidates.dates: Event nights from the official schedule: Fri 18 Dec (Steve Angello), Sat 19 Dec (ESSENCE, they are in Hakone), Sat 26 Dec (NEON STARS), plus a 12.29 TUE ESSENCE listing (check whether it means the night of Mon 28). No event is listed for Sun 27 or Mon 28.
candidates.price: Not on the site. Advance tickets are on zaiko.io / livepocket.jp per event; guides put Tokyo club covers at about ¥2,000–5,000. Buy advance for Steve Angello.
candidates.booking: Buy advance tickets on zaiko/livepocket from the event page once on sale. VIP tables can be booked on the site (Book VIP), and a table could suit 8 if split.
candidates.group_of_8: Yes, a huge venue. Everyone needs their own original passport at the door.
candidates.hours: Google: Thu–Sun 23:00–04:30, closed Mon–Wed (event nights may differ)
candidates.first_last: Last trains leave around 00:00–00:30, so either stay until the first trains (about 05:00) or take taxis. From Garfield House it is a walk home.

evidence.note: December lineup: 12.18 FRI THE ONE Presents Steve Angello; 12.19 SAT ESSENCE; 12.26 SAT NEON STARS; 12.29 TUE ESSENCE; tickets via zaiko/livepocket

Entry is 20+ only, with an ID check for everyone: passport, driver's licence or residence card. No photos, copies or expired IDs. Tank tops, sleeveless tops and sandals may be refused, and very drunk guests are turned away.
4.5 from 1,493 ratings, operational, Thu–Sun 23:00–04:30
Calls it the Kabukicho club known for sheer scale; clubs strictly enforce 20+ and want a passport

candidates.name: Shinjuku Kabuki Hall / Kabuki Yokocho
candidates.name_ja: 新宿カブキhall～歌舞伎横丁
candidates.why: A loud, neon food-festival hall with 10 stalls from around Japan and Korea, plus nightly music and video shows. It is the easiest place to sit 8 people together at short notice, and it is right below ZEROTOKYO, so it works as the pre-game before the club.
candidates.best_time: 20:00–23:00 before the club, or 03:00+ as a refuel
candidates.dates: Open daily; no year-end notice on the site
candidates.price: Pay per stall; the Kabukicho Tower BBQ beer garden plan (¥6,600 with free-flow drinks) is for groups of 50+ only, so ignore it
candidates.booking: Walk in. The hall takes reservations for groups of 10 or more, so 8 can just turn up.
candidates.group_of_8: Yes, the best walk-in option in Shinjuku for 8

evidence.note: 10 stalls in 1,000 m² on 2F, nightly performances, groups of 10 to 1,000 accepted, smaller groups welcome

candidates.name: Shinjuku Golden Gai
candidates.why: About 200 micro-bars across six alleys, the classic Tokyo bar crawl. Most bars seat only 6–8 people, so split into two groups of 4 and hop. Pick bars that post English prices outside and walk past ones marked 'regulars only'.
candidates.best_time: 21:00–01:00, between dinner and the club; Sun 27 or Mon 28 are calmer
candidates.dates: Most bars are open nightly; some small bars close for the holidays from about 29–31 Dec, so go before 29 Dec
candidates.price: Seat charge usually ¥500–1,500 per person (sometimes it includes the first drink), and drinks about ¥700–1,000. Mostly cash only.
candidates.booking: No booking. Walk in, and move on if the bar is full.
candidates.group_of_8: Only if you split into groups of 3–4 across neighbouring bars
candidates.first_last: 5 minutes from Garfield House on foot

evidence.note: Expect ¥500–¥1,500 per person, often including the first drink; keep groups small

candidates.best_time: 17:30–20:00, before the stalls fill with after-work drinkers
candidates.dates: Busy with year-end office parties (bōnenkai) in mid-December; some stalls close from about 29–31 Dec
candidates.price: Budget: skewers about ¥200–400, beer about ¥600–700 (typical; not verified for each stall)
candidates.group_of_8: Only if you split across two stalls
candidates.hours: Stall by stall, mostly late afternoon to about midnight
candidates.first_last: Next to JR Shinjuku West Exit

notes: Tokyo · night: Two bases set the night logic. NIGHTS 15–18 DEC (Ninja House, Toshima): stay local on Tue 15 (arrival) and Wed 16. Daitokai (24h, beer about ¥250) and Wakadaisho by the West and North Exits, then Round1 Ikebukuro (24h bowling, karaoke and arcade) or Big Echo West Exit (until 06:00 on Fri and Sat); all within walking distance of the stay. Thu 17: Shibuya or Ebisu (Ebisu Yokocho, Shibuya Yokocho). FRI 18 DEC is the big night and peak year-end office party (bōnenkai) season, so izakaya fill early: book any sit-down for 8. Headline: ZEROTOKYO Steve Angello (buy advance tickets). Take taxis or wait for the first trains back to Toshima, and keep the 19 Dec Hakone departure in mind. NIGHTS 26–28 DEC (Garfield House, Shinjuku): everything is walkable. Sat 26: Omoide Yokocho, then Kabuki Hall (seats 8 walk-in), then ZEROTOKYO NEON STARS, then Nagi ramen (24h). Sun 27 and Mon 28: ZEROTOKYO (Mon–Wed per Google) and WOMB (Sun/Mon) are closed, so do Umi no Ie unlimited nomihodai (¥1,480) and Golden Gai in groups of 4, then ATOM Shibuya (open nightly, men ¥900 before 23:30) or Karaokekan Kabukicho (until 06:00). YEAR-END: chains, clubs, karaoke and Round1 run normally through 28 Dec; small Golden Gai and Omoide stalls may start closing from about 29 Dec. Mon 28 is the last safe night. The flight is 17:20 on 29 Dec, so leave Shinjuku by about 14:00. ID: every club is strictly 20+ and wants the ORIGINAL passport (no photos or copies); no sandals, tank tops or sports pants. Last trains run about 00:00–00:30, so plan to party until the first train (about 05:00) or split taxis.
